title: Communication Reflection - 2026-06-05

coverage: Meet transcript entries: 5 across 1 meeting transcript
topics: Captioning and accessibility work for a launch video.
Workflow feedback around a proof-of-concept production fix.
Decision clarity around final delivery versus backup edits.
Ownership clarity before applying a note across related shots.
Review judgement around whether a technically successful result matches the intended look.

thingsDoneWell: You translated a vague captioning request into an implementable delivery detail by providing an SRT file and naming how captions would work across platforms.
You asked for specific process feedback rather than general approval. That makes the proof of concept easier to evaluate.
You made a pragmatic delivery call by suggesting the team skip backup edits when the final version was ready.

paragraphs: The main improvement area is ownership clarity. You identified that a note may be valid, and the next message should name who decides whether it applies across all related shots.
The proof-of-concept thread is ready for more structure. It needs success criteria, approval state, and an owner if it is becoming a repeatable workflow.
examples: Owner wrapper: this note is valid, but we need one owner to decide whether it applies across all related shots.
Process wrapper: please give feedback on visual quality, time saved, repeatability, and any approval concerns.
Delivery wrapper: if the final version is approved, we can skip backup edit variants and deliver the final.

followUps: Confirm whether the SRT caption workflow works on the target platforms.
Collect proof-of-concept feedback on quality, time saved, and repeatability.
Assign an owner for deciding whether the note applies across related shots.
Confirm whether backup edits can be removed from the delivery path.
Document the proof-of-concept workflow if it becomes repeatable.
Decide whether the technically successful result is acceptable for the intended look.

paragraphs: High conscientiousness shows up in the captioning detail and the desire to make a workflow repeatable rather than treating it as a one-off fix.
High open-mindedness shows up in the willingness to test a new workflow and ask whether it can become a broader production capability.
High assertiveness helps you move the team toward a decision, especially around skipping backup edits and identifying ownership gaps.
examples: Conscientiousness: turning captions into an SRT/platform compatibility question.
Open-mindedness: testing whether a proof of concept can generalise into a repeatable workflow.
Assertiveness: proposing a clear delivery path when finals are ready.
Agreeableness: asking for feedback in a way that invites collaborators into the process.

overallSentiment: The day reads as practical and constructive, with communication focused on finishing work and turning experiments into usable process.
The coaching watch-out is to add explicit ownership and approval state when a promising experiment starts becoming a real workflow.
